sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Origin**: Launched in 2008 by the **World Bank** to assist developing countries in their REDD+ efforts.
• **Core Objective**: To build capacity for REDD+ activities and test performance-based payment systems for emission reductions.
• **Operational Structure**: Comprises two separate but complementary mechanisms: the **Readiness Fund** and the **Carbon Fund**.
• **Key Metric**: **Emission Reductions (ERs)** measured in tonnes of CO2 equivalent, verified against a national or sub-national reference level.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Provides grants to build national systems (MRV, reference levels, strategies).
Capacity building and policy framework development.
Provides performance-based payments for verified emission reductions.

items.definition: Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation. The '+' includes conservation, sustainable management, and enhancement of forest carbon stocks.
Measurement, Reporting, and Verification. The technical backbone required to quantify forest carbon and ensure environmental integrity.
Benchmarks against which the performance of REDD+ activities is measured to determine the amount of emission reductions achieved.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Readiness Preparation Proposal (R-PP)**: A document outlining how a country plans to prepare for REDD+.
• **Emission Reductions Payment Agreement (ERPA)**: Legal contract between the FCPF Carbon Fund and a country to purchase verified emission reductions.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: High transaction costs, complex MRV requirements, and issues regarding land tenure and benefit-sharing.
• **Solutions**: Scaling up private sector finance and integrating nature-based solutions into national climate policies.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'FCPF = R + C'
• **Decoded Meaning**: FCPF is the sum of **R**eadiness (Grants for capacity) and **C**arbon (Payments for results).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: FCPF is NOT a UN body; it is a World Bank-hosted partnership. Do not confuse it with the Green Climate Fund (GCF) or the Clean Development Mechanism (CDM).
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Results-Based Financing' (RBF) when discussing climate finance to demonstrate depth of understanding.

keyTakeaways: FCPF is a World Bank initiative supporting REDD+ readiness and implementation.
It operates through two funds: Readiness Fund (capacity) and Carbon Fund (performance-based payments).
It is critical for developing countries to transition from deforestation to sustainable forest management.
